note: Rewritten from Hagen 1858, the original Latin description plus a detailed German account (Monographie der Termiten; this species is no. 39). Type locality Santarem (Amazon River), consistent with "Brasil: Pará: Santarém" in the entry page; the collector Bates records that the species swarms at midday on overcast days, and that the nest is a very small conical carton nest among twigs and grass roots, small enough to be covered by one hand. The original describes only the alate; the soldier is unknown. The German "Long. c. alis 6½ mill." is transcribed as 6.5 mm; the OCR corrupts forms such as antcnnis, capile and Prolhorax, and the translation reads them by context. Nest and swarming behaviour are biological records and are not expanded here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Originally described as Termes exiguus. The shape and body colour are very similar to T. debilis, but the species is much smaller; the head is more arched and longer, with a small tubercle in the middle of the frons; the broad anterior margin is not pressed down but has a distinct semicircular incision; the compound eyes are less projecting, and the ocelli are as in T. debilis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Jet black to blackish brown; antennae brown with pale rings; legs brown with dark knees; abdomen brown, with a pale band at the tip of the ventral surface and in the middle of the base; wings opaque, greyish white, with a black costa. Head arched, elongate-oval, with a small tubercle in the middle of the frons; ocelli small, close to the compound eyes; pronotum small and rounded. Head and pronotum shining black; mouthparts, antennae and legs pale brown, the antennal rings paler and the knees of the legs darker; body brown, with a pale longitudinal stripe at the tip of the ventral surface and in the middle of the base; wings dark, greyish white, with a black marginal vein. The head is more strongly arched and longer, with a small tubercle on the frons; the broad anterior margin is not pressed down but forms a very strong semicircular incision; the compound eyes project less, and the ocelli are as in T. debilis. The antennae are as long as the head, with 13 segments, stout and progressively thicker towards the tip; the two basal segments are cylindrical, segment 2 shorter, the next two segments small and ring-like, the remaining segments spherical and the last oval. The pronotum is shaped as in T. debilis but flattened, its anterior margin scarcely curled upwards and its anterior corners not pressed down; a groove runs back from the anterior margin along the midline, beginning at a rather deep pit. The abdomen is as in T. debilis, with a very small abdominal process. The wings are as in T. debilis, the media forked in the distal third, the submedia with about 7 branches. Measurements: body length with wings 6.5 mm; body length 3 mm; wing span 11 mm.
